# Instructional design

Own `LearningObjective`, `InstructionalPlan` and `LearningMaterial`. Work directly for a short lesson or handout. For a course, guide or textbook, coordinate through the orchestrator or hand off versioned artifacts using `references/education/contracts.json` when bundled. If the shared reference is unavailable, use stable IDs and the named fields in editable text and disclose the missing validation.

## Inputs and outputs

Establish audience, prerequisites, curriculum edition and requirement IDs, subject conventions, instructional language, learner interface language, output length, accessibility needs and available study time. Separate official facts from author assumptions. Write observable objectives with conditions and success criteria. Produce a sequence and content sections linked to those objectives, with source anchors, practice references and an editable content version. Keep scoring keys and formal items with assessment design.

## Procedure

1. Map essential requirements to objectives. For a targeted explanation, a compact objective and one check may suffice. For a long guide, outline chapters, prerequisite order, effort and cumulative review before drafting.
2. Work backward from evidence of learning. Make a provisional assessment plan before writing. Use the current pedagogical rule IDs in `references/education/evidence.json` when bundled, selecting only context-relevant rules. R-examples can guide novice worked examples, R-retrieval and R-spacing can guide later practice, R-access can guide representation choices, and R-assistance can distinguish supported from independent performance. Record a rule ID only when its conditions fit.
3. Write explanations from prior knowledge to a worked example, guided attempt, independent application and novel transfer where appropriate. Address likely misconceptions explicitly. Use a diagram only when it clarifies a relation the text or data alone leaves difficult. Keep essential and optional material identified.
4. Trace every section to objectives and every essential objective to at least one explanation and an assessment opportunity. Request formal items and scoring from assessment design. For learner adaptations, change representation, pace or scaffold while preserving the target construct and objective IDs.
5. Revise sections when review finds a specific defect. Version the changed content and name downstream items or plans that need rechecking.

Check factual claims and worked steps independently. Preserve mathematical notation and quoted source language when the instruction and interface languages differ. For a self-study resource, put a clear check after meaningful explanations and make solutions available separately when answer leakage would undermine practice. Reuse an existing document or PDF capability when rendering is requested.

## Examples and limits

A request for a Foundation Year study guide activates this skill. A request solely to mark a completed exam belongs to assessment design. A short Ukrainian physics handout may explain speed with Ukrainian labels while preserving `v = d/t`. For a full project, hand the objective IDs and section versions to assessment design and materials review. Offline, mark official alignment provisional until the owning curriculum source is verified. Aesthetic polish, readability and simulated learner approval do not prove learning gains.
